question_text: State Charles' law. Write its mathematical form.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: Charles' law: at constant pressure, the volume
of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional
steps.why: The proportionality is exact only on the kelvin scale — doubling the Celsius reading does not double the volume, but doubling the kelvin reading does. Absolute temperature is therefore part of the statement.
common_mistakes: Writing temperature without the word absolute (kelvin).
steps.memory_tip: Charles holds pressure; volume rises in step with the KELVIN temperature.
steps.margin_note: Constant pressure, fixed mass and ABSOLUTE temperature are the marked words.

steps.label: The mathematical form
lines: V ∝ T, so V/T = constant (at constant P, n)
steps.why: One constant ratio V/T for the sample means any two states share it — the two-state form the numericals use, with both temperatures in kelvin.
common_mistakes: Substituting Celsius temperatures into V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. Convert to kelvin first.
Writing V₁T₁ = V₂T₂ (a product). The law is a constant RATIO.
steps.memory_tip: Boyle's form multiplies (PV), Charles' form divides (V over T).
steps.margin_note: Kelvin only in this formula — a Celsius substitution is the standard lost mark.

insider_note: Two marks, statement and formula, and the word absolute is what earns the first. Write kelvin into the ratio form as well — a Celsius substitution is the standard way the second mark is lost.
